results.fact: approach routed via Cascade Pass in waypoints, but never mentioned in the approach prose
results.correct_value: The approach leaves the road by the Cascade Pass trailhead and crosses the Cascade River and moraine directly to the C-J couloir; it does not go up to Cascade Pass.
results.evidence: Still real in the live row: waypoints[1] is 'Cascade Pass' (distMi 3.6), and the river crossing, couloir base and hanging-glacier pins carry distMi 4.3/4.8/5.5 measured via the pass, while the approach, approach_variants and the trailhead pin's own directions have the party walk back down the road and cross the river directly, on route within an hour of the car. The fact was settled by the first pass (couloir apron about 20 minutes from the road); the fix is removing the Cascade Pass pin and re-measuring the later distMi, which is pin work and would require computed distances. Left for the pin pass.

results.fact: Elevation/location of the route's rock-chimney crux
results.evidence: Still real: beta and rope_note put a short rock chimney near 5,100 ft, while turnaround and detailed_rack call it the 'summit chimney'. On retry, a scramble report's summary places a brief, tricky chimney-gully between the south peak and Melakwa Lake (low on the route), and a 2019 report describes only a gully at the start of the summit scramble with large jugs; the other trip reports that were readable do not mention a chimney. Still no two sources give the chimney's position, so no field is changed.

results.fact: Mileage along the PCT to the stump/boot-path turnoff (4.6-5 mi vs 5.5-6 mi vs mile 5.75)
results.evidence: Still real: beta and pitch_detail say 4.6-5 mi one way, approach, approach_variants and descent_text say ~5.5-6 mi, the itinerary says mile 5.75, and partner_requirements ~11 mi round trip. New sources only widen the spread: one description has the summit an easy scramble after about four miles of PCT, another calls it about 5 miles one way, while the earlier figures were 9.2 mi and ~11 mi round trip. No two sources agree on the turnoff's mileage.

results.fact: Length of the downclimb at the Grotesque Gendarmes
results.evidence: The two figures measure different things. The trip report behind both describes descending about 150 ft down a prominent buttress, then a narrow gully for another ~50 ft, then another ~50 ft to an easier ledge, for a total descent of 250-300 ft. The row's ~150 ft (beta, pitch_detail[1], detailed_rack) is the buttress downclimb followed by the gully, and its 250-300 ft (hazards, the gendarmes waypoint, descent) is the whole bypass.

Both Klawatti rows still credit Anderson, Boyer and Gorton (July 7, 1940) as this route's first ascent. The only source naming a route for that party remains the one route database that lists it under the SW Buttress (a search result repeats it). A winter-ascent report on the peak discusses the south face, SW ridge and west face without saying which the 1940 party used; the peak's main route page and an FA chronology page could not be fetched. No second source ties the 1940 party to a line.

Same as the SW Buttress row: the Southeast Face row's `fa` also names the 1940 Anderson/Boyer/Gorton party as its first ascent. Only one route database assigns that party to a line (the SW Buttress), and no second source confirms which route they climbed, so neither row's `fa` is changed.

results.fact: Total elevation gain and loss for the round trip
results.evidence: Still real: gain_ft 6120 and loss_ft 9500, the itinerary days summing to 7,000 up and down, and totalNote saying ~9,500. New figures do not converge: a trip report gives 29.2 mi round trip with only an elevation range (2,080-8,200 ft); a search summary cites ~30 mi and ~7,500 ft from another report; the earlier ~9,500 ft figure included a side trip to White Mountain. No two sources state the same cumulative gain.

results.fact: Which side of the peak the route climbs from the gap (east ridge/face vs southwest slopes 'staying left of the broad west ridge')
results.evidence: Retry searches of Necklace Valley and La Bohn Gap trip reports found only that La Bohn Peak is a short (about 700 ft), straightforward solid-rock scramble from La Bohn Gap / La Bohn Lakes camp, with no side or ridge named. Nothing new settles whether the line is the east ridge or the southwest slopes, so the row's descriptions are not rewritten.

results.fact: Total elevation gain for the route
results.evidence: Still real: gain_ft 1500 against the itinerary's '~9,000+ ft' for day 1 alone. New sources: a report of Le Conte plus Hurry-Up from the Cascade Pass trailhead gives 26.2 mi round trip and only an elevation range (3,650-7,821 ft); a traverse party gives 16.5 mi / 7.8k ft to a camp 1,000 ft above Yang Yang Lakes, but that included a 3-mile road walk; a search summary cites 12 mi / 5.5k ft trailhead to Yang Yang Lakes from one report. None gives a car-to-car Le Conte total, and the day-1 figures do not agree.

results.fact: Elevation of the glacier-exit / moat transition below the col
results.evidence: Still as before: the prose's ~6,200 ft is where the line exits left up a short cliff step onto the glacial remnants, while the 6,500 ft waypoint names a snow-gully top / moat transition, and seasonal_hazards places the moat at the col. Sources place the moat differently (just below the notch above 7,200 ft; halfway up the steep snow), so the waypoint may be a different feature from the 6,200 ft exit. No new source gives an elevation for it.
